key_insight: ARC performance depends strongly on both pretraining and test-time training budgets, not just model architecture, with TRM and VARC responding differently to these controls.
engineering_relevance: For fair ARC benchmarking and model selection, engineers should report and compare pretraining and TTT budgets at matched settings rather than attributing gains solely to architecture.
method: Crossed 5 pretraining budgets with 4 test-time training budgets per test task
Compared vision-inspired VARC and recursion-based TRM under the same inductive ARC-AGI-1 protocol
Varied task-variant count and total sample presentations as controlled training budgets
evidence_signal: Across ARC-AGI-1 evaluations, more TTT sample presentations improved pass@2 for both models, while more task variants helped TRM consistently but often hurt VARC.
watch_item: Results are budget-sensitive, so conclusions can be misleading if pretraining data, augmentation, or TTT setup are not matched across models.
paper_title: Pretraining and Test-Time Training Budgets Matter for ARC: A Controlled Study of VARC and TRM
